title: Bigger AI isn't always better for your business
summary: The biggest AI models grab the headlines, but everyday jobs like answering calls and booking appointments often run better on smaller, focused AI. Here's how to think about it.
keyTakeaways: Big, general AI models are built to do everything. Most business tasks need one thing done well.
Smaller, focused AI is often faster and cheaper to run, which matters on a live phone call.
Many good systems use both: a light model for routine work and a bigger one for the hard questions.
Choose AI by the job it does for you, not by how famous the model is.

content.heading: The headline race
body: Every few months a new, bigger AI model makes the news. These models are impressive: they can write essays, summarise long reports and help write software.
But your front desk doesn't need to write poetry. It needs to answer the phone, understand what the caller wants and book them in, quickly and correctly, hundreds of times a week.

content.heading: Why focus often wins
body: For everyday business jobs, a smaller AI that's set up for one task can be the better choice.
points: Speed: on a phone call, a quick reply matters more than a clever one
Cost: you pay for every conversation, so a lighter model can cost much less to run
Consistency: a focused setup is easier to keep on script, with your prices, your policies and your tone

content.heading: When bigger is worth it
body: Bigger models still earn their place. Reading a long contract, handling an unusual complaint or answering a question nobody planned for can need more thinking power.

That's why many good systems use both. A light, fast model handles the routine calls and messages, and hands over to a more powerful one only when a conversation needs it. You get speed most of the time and depth when it counts.

content.heading: Questions to ask any AI provider
body: You don't need to know model names to make a good choice. Ask questions about results instead.
points: How quickly does it reply on a real call?
What does each conversation cost us?
How does it stick to our information instead of guessing?
What happens when it doesn't know the answer?

content.heading: The takeaway
body: The best AI for your business is the one that does your job well at a sensible cost, not the one with the biggest headline. When Deptloy builds a system, we pick the AI for each task, so you're not paying for power you'll never use.
